title: Memoria
summary: Memoria is a cyberpunk-flavoured comic story by Stefan "Twoflower" Gagne, first published in 1994 as part of the "A Future We'd Like to See" series. The narrator is Rynard Lopwagen, a brash, underachieving teenager who talks his way into a research project run by the ailing, immortality-seeking Mr. Rinhurst. The team has an unbreakable encrypted archive, along with a preserved piece of a human brain that stores the autobiography of a dead biotech doctor, Filbert Whack-A-Doo. The brain's interactive hologram of Filbert will only reveal his "secret of immortality" after Rynard answers a series of questions about his life. Rynard reads the autobiography, a slangy, irreverent account of Filbert's youth, career and personal regrets, while a rival scientist, Martin McDoole, grows impatient. The story is light and jokey, full of period slang and pop-culture references, and it builds to a warm, reflective conclusion about how people live on through the memories and impact they leave in others.
